title: The typed nil error
hints: Check returns an error even for valid input. Look at its return type: it returns a *CheckError variable through the error interface.

A nil *CheckError converted to error is a non-nil interface holding a nil pointer, the same trap as in interfaces_03. Functions should declare their result as error and return a literal nil on success.
Return nil explicitly when there is no problem, for example: if len(problems) == 0 { return nil }; return &CheckError{Problems: problems}.
